subject: MSA redlines — security exhibit fallback & evidence cadence
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clarionhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Leary <ben.leary@clarionhealth.com>, external-legal@clarionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: MSA redlines - security exhibit questions and proposed fallback

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for sending the MSA and exhibit. Our legal and infosec teams reviewed and have three areas they want clarified before we can sign: 

1) Pen test window and scope — we need explicit language on who can run tests, required notifications, and acceptable staging vs prod carve-outs.
2) SOC 2 attestation timeline — we’d like assurance the next attestations will be delivered within 90 days of request and an SLA for when evidence will be available.
3) Fallback model / continuity — if Redwood substitutes a smaller model for capacity reasons, we need clear fallback guarantees and notification cadence.

I attached a redline (clarion_MSA_redlines_v2.docx) with inline comments. High level asks: align the pen test clause to our standard notice periods (7 business days for non-intrusive, 14 for intrusive), a commitments table for evidence delivery, and a short fallback escalation path.

Can we get proposed language by EOD Friday 11/13? If not, please suggest an alternative cadence.

Cheers,
Emily Zhao
Director, Vendor Risk & Privacy
Clarion Health

Attachment: clarion_MSA_redlines_v2.docx (docx)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - security exhibit questions and proposed fallback

Hi Emily — thanks for the detailed review and the redlines. Tagging Karthik (legal) and Olga (assurance) so we can coordinate proposed edits.

Quick notes / plan:
- Pen test language: we can accept the 7 / 14 business day notice bands with a short exception for emergency CVE-driven tests (we propose same-week notice to our security on-call plus a post-test report).
- SOC 2 / evidence: we typically surface attestation PDFs within 30 days of request for current-year reports; for historical artifacts we propose a request SLA of 10 business days for SOC 2 mapping docs and 30 business days for rolling logs/longer artifacts. We will include an evidence commitments table in the draft.
- Fallback model: we want to avoid prescriptive model names in contract. Proposed approach: (a) define "compatible model variant" with an objective similarity threshold, (b) 24-hour notice for scheduled fallback and 1-hour notification for automated failover with an opt-in SLA extension for customers that require guaranteed model parity.

Action items: I’ll circulate a proposed redline by Thursday 11/12 EOD to keep to your timeline. If that slips, we’ll aim for Monday 11/16 and can set a 30-min sync.

Short question for you — on the evidence table, do you require continuous access to logs (read-only API) or periodic bundles? That will affect our recommended SLA language.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Leary <ben.leary@clarionhealth.com>

> - SOC 2 / evidence: we typically surface attestation PDFs within 30 days of request for current-year reports; for historical artifacts we propose a request SLA of 10 business days for SOC 2 mapping docs and 30 business days for rolling logs/longer artifacts. We will include an evidence commitments table in the draft.
> - Fallback model: we want to avoid prescriptive model names in contract. Proposed approach: (a) define "compatible model variant" with an objective similarity threshold, (b) 24-hour notice for scheduled fallback and 1-hour notification for automated failover with an opt-in SLA extension for customers that require guaranteed model parity.

Thanks Jasmine — that looks reasonable. To Emily’s question on log access: Clarion’s compliance team prefers a read-only API feed for token-level audit logs on demand (monthly or by request) rather than periodic bundles. That gives them the ability to pull when they need and tie to internal monitoring.

Minor ask: can Redwood add a bullet in the evidence commitments table that clarifies retained retention windows for ephemeral logs vs aggregated metrics? That will unblock our procurement.

Ben
VP, Procurement Operations
Clarion Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clarionhealth.com>, Ben Leary <ben.leary@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - security exhibit questions and proposed fallback

Hi Emily / Ben — following up with the proposed edits attached and a short implementation playbook. Summary of changes in the attachment (security-exhibit-diff.pdf):

• Pen test clause: updated to 7 / 14 business day notice bands, emergency CVE exception with post-test report requirement, and a requirement to coordinate test plans with Redwood staging team for intrusive tests.
• Evidence commitments table: added read-only API option for token-level audit log pulls (monthly or by request), retention windows called out (30 days ephemeral tokens, 365 days aggregated metrics), and explicit SOC 2 attestation delivery timelines (30 days for current-year, 45 days max for queued requests).
• Fallback / model substitution: defined "compatible model variant" with objective similarity checks (latency within 1.5x and top-K output overlap threshold), 24-hour notice for planned substitutions, 1-hour incident notification, and an opt-in SLA for model parity (addendum).

Next steps:
1) Review the attached PDF redline and confirm any higher-priority asks we should escalate to product/legal.
2) If acceptable, we’ll fold the language into the MSA redline docx and send back to you for signatures (we can also route the parity addendum as a separate order-form attachment if you prefer).
3) If you need a short call, Karthik and Olga are available Thu 11/19 9–11am PT.

Attachments: security-exhibit-diff.pdf (pdf), clarion_MSA_redlines_v2.docx (docx)

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Counsel, Redwood Inference
